brief_summary: Two-panel cross-section: left panel shows the /dev/tty dye-sub PBT construction as a single mold cavity with dye sublimated into the surface, paired with a short 'lower tooling cost' bar; right panel shows a generic double-shot ABS construction with a dedicated second-shot legend cavity, paired with a taller 'higher tooling cost' bar in the caution color. Illustrates the article's stated reason the 2017 run shipped dye-sub rather than double-shot.
data_sources: data/keycap-sets/mt3-devtty.json — description: 'Double-shot ABS retooling came later, on other Drop MT3 releases — the 2017 /dev/tty run itself shipped dye-sub to avoid the far higher tooling cost of double-shot legends.'
mt3-devtty-restock.mdx § 'Why dye-sub, not double-shot' — restates the tooling-cost tradeoff qualitatively; no specific cost figures are asserted, per the no-fabrication rule.
warnings: Cost bars are qualitative (relative height only, no dollar figures) since the catalog record and article give no numeric tooling-cost figure.
